clinical.citation: Clinical, molecular and glycophenotype insights in SLC39A8-CDG (PMID: 34246313)

phenotypes: severe developmental disability
dystonic postural pattern and dyskinesia
Leigh syndrome-like neuroimaging (basal ganglia, thalami, white matter)
cerebral and cerebellar atrophy
variable or near-normal transferrin IEF (slight increase of trisialotransferrin)
hypogalactosylated transferrin N-glycans on MALDI-MS in one sibling, spontaneously decreasing over time
undergalactosylated and undersialylated serum N-glycans (increased A2G1S1)

phenotypes: severe developmental disability

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Novel biallelic SLC39A8 variants in two siblings with a phenotype consistent with SLC39A8-CDG (clinical, MRI and glycomic features). Homozygous A391T in a third patient with overlapping features.

clinical.citation: The schizophrenia risk locus in SLC39A8 alters brain metal transport and plasma glycosylation (PMID: 32753748)

variants.description: p.Ala391Thr (rs13107325), common missense allele; human carriers (dose-dependent, including heterozygotes)
phenotypes: dose-dependent change in brain MRI T2w/T1w signal ratio in several regions
specific reduction of serum manganese
reduced complexity and branching of plasma N-glycans
schizophrenia risk allele

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Common schizophrenia-associated missense variant shown to be hypofunctional: lower serum Mn, altered plasma N-glycome and brain MRI changes in carriers. Two individuals with SLC39A8-CDG were also profiled and had more severe glycosylation changes that improved with Mn supplementation.

clinical.citation: A missense variant in SLC39A8 is associated with severe idiopathic scoliosis (PMID: 30301978)

phenotypes: severe adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
greater spinal curvature
decreased height
increased BMI
lower plasma manganese

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Exome-wide association in 457 severe AIS cases (discovery) plus 841 cases (replication) versus controls (combined P = 7.02e-14, OR 1.94); reduced Mn influx by the variant in functional studies; slc39a8 mutant zebrafish show vertebral abnormalities.

model_organism.citation: Lin et al. 2018 - Zinc transporter Slc39a8 is essential for cardiac ventricular compaction (PMID: 29337306)
phenotypes: Homozygous null embryos do not survive embryogenesis
Cardiac phenotype similar to human left ventricular noncompaction (excessive trabeculation, impaired compaction)
Slc39a8 expressed in endothelial cells of the developing heart, where it maintains cellular Zn levels
Marked ECM accumulation in null hearts
Reduced expression of several Adamts metalloproteinases
SLC39A8 knockdown in HUVECs decreased ADAMTS1 transcription via reduced Zn uptake and MTF1 activity

model_organism.citation: In utero gene expression in the Slc39a8(neo/neo) knockdown mouse (PMID: 30013175)
phenotypes: ZIP8 mRNA and protein at 10-15% of wild-type
Stunted growth
Neonatal lethality
Multi-organ dysmorphogenesis
Dysregulated hematopoiesis with severe anemia
RNA-seq of GD13.5 yolk sac/placenta and GD16.5 tissues showed 29 unique DEGs enriched for hematopoiesis, hypoxia, complement and coagulation categories
Altered zinc-finger/GATA-related transcription factor targets, predominantly in yolk sac

model_organism.citation: Generation of a Slc39a8 hypomorph mouse: markedly decreased ZIP8 Zn2+/(HCO3-)2 transporter expression (PMID: 21658371)
phenotypes: Slc39a8(neo) hypomorphic allele
Slc39a8(neo/neo) homozygotes show dramatically decreased ZIP8 expression in embryo, fetus and visceral yolk sac
Cre recombinase did not function in the intact mouse

model_organism.citation: Metal-ion transporter SLC39A8 is required for brain manganese uptake and accumulation (PMID: 37482277)
phenotypes: Inducible global Slc39a8 KO crossed with Slc39a14 KO
Markedly decreased brain Mn loading despite systemic hypermanganesemia and increased bone and kidney Mn
Other divalent metals in brain unaffected
54Mn uptake impaired in brain but not most other tissues
Slc39a8 inactivation efficient in brain microvessels but not choroid plexus, suggesting blood-brain barrier uptake

model_organism.citation: Neuronal SLC39A8 deficiency impairs cerebellar development by altering manganese homeostasis (PMID: 39435657)
phenotypes: Neuron-specific KO (Slc39a8-NSKO) with markedly decreased Mn in whole brain, especially cerebellum
Impaired brain 54Mn uptake
Cerebellar morphological defects
Abnormal Purkinje cell dendritic arborization
Reduced neurogenesis and increased apoptosis in the external granular layer
Motor dysfunction
Downregulation of neurodevelopment, synaptic plasticity and cAMP signaling pathway genes

model_organism.citation: The manganese transporter SLC39A8 links alkaline ceramidase 1 to inflammatory bowel disease (PMID: 38839750)
phenotypes: Intestinal epithelial cell-specific KO with markedly decreased Mn in blood and most organs
Impaired intestinal absorption of dietary Mn
Barrier dysfunction
Upregulated alkaline ceramidase 1 (ACER1)
ACER1 inhibitor attenuated colitis

model_organism.citation: A missense variant in SLC39A8 is associated with severe idiopathic scoliosis (PMID: 30301978)
phenotypes: slc39a8 mutant zebrafish show vertebral abnormalities
Impaired growth
Decreased motor activity

model_organism.citation: A mouse model characterizes the roles of ZIP8 in systemic iron recycling and lung inflammation and infection (PMID: 36260707)
phenotypes: Global inducible ZIP8 KO
Elevated spleen iron and decreased serum iron, suggesting a role in iron recycling
ZIP8 expressed on lung distal airspace epithelial cells and transports iron from airway into lung tissue
No effect on severity of LPS-induced acute lung injury
No effect on outcome of Klebsiella pneumoniae infection

model_organism.citation: Intestinal ZIP8 Regulates Tissue Manganese Distribution and Modifies Manganese Overload in ZIP14 Deficiency (PMID: 41394108)
phenotypes: Intestine-specific Zip8 KO did not change basal blood Mn
Reduced liver and bone Mn
In Zip14-/- background, reduced blood and brain Mn in female double KO mice only (sex-specific)
Bone Mn remained elevated in all groups

model_organism.citation: SLC39A8-mediated zinc dyshomeostasis potentiates kidney disease (PMID: 40956895)
phenotypes: Kidney-specific Slc39a8 KO (and A391T knock-in) showed reduced renal zinc accumulation
Reduced susceptibility to kidney injury and disease progression
Activation of zinc-AKT-FOXO1-G6PC axis
EDTA zinc chelation recapitulated protection

biological.citation: Wang et al. 2025 - SLC39A8-mediated zinc dyshomeostasis potentiates kidney disease (PMID: 40956895)
biological.summary: Large-cohort screening identified the SLC39A8 A391T variant (rs13107325) as a shared modifier of multiple kidney diseases. A391T knock-in and kidney-specific Slc39a8 knockout mice had reduced renal zinc and were protected from kidney injury, acting through the zinc-AKT-FOXO1-G6PC axis. EDTA zinc chelation reproduced the protection in acute and chronic kidney disease models.

biological.citation: The ZIP8/SIRT1 axis regulates alveolar progenitor cell renewal in aging and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (PMID: 35389887)
biological.summary: ZIP8 expression was reduced in AEC2s from IPF lungs and aged mouse lungs. AEC2-specific Zip8 deletion impaired renewal, increased bleomycin sensitivity and caused spontaneous fibrosis. ZIP8 acts through SIRT1, and zinc plus SIRT1 activation restored AEC2 self-renewal in cells from IPF patients and old mice.

biological.citation: SLC39A8 deficiency: biochemical correction and major clinical improvement by manganese therapy (PMID: 28749473)
biological.summary: SLC39A8 deficiency causes manganese deficiency and a congenital disorder of glycosylation because Mn-dependent β-1,4-galactosyltransferases fail. High-dose MnSO4 in two patients normalized the glycosylation enzyme defects and improved motor, hearing and neurological function.

biological.citation: The schizophrenia-associated variant in SLC39A8 alters protein glycosylation in the mouse brain (PMID: 35260802)
biological.summary: In A391T homozygous knock-in mice, brain N-glycosylation was impaired in a region-dependent manner, and about one-third of detected cortical glycoproteins were differentially N-glycosylated. These included cell adhesion molecules and neurotransmitter receptors. RNAseq showed little regional change, pointing to altered glycosylation enzyme activity rather than altered gene expression.

biological.citation: The schizophrenia risk locus in SLC39A8 alters brain metal transport and plasma glycosylation (PMID: 32753748)
biological.summary: Carriers of the common SLC39A8 missense allele (A391T) showed a dose-dependent change in brain MRI T2w/T1w signal ratio, a specific reduction in serum Mn, and reduced complexity and branching of plasma N-glycans. Two SLC39A8-CDG patients had similar but more severe glycan changes that improved with Mn supplementation, suggesting a spectrum of hypofunction.

biological.citation: Co-expression analysis reveals interpretable gene modules controlled by trans-acting genetic variants (PMID: 32880574)
biological.summary: A trans-eQTL near SLC39A8 regulates a metallothionein gene module in LPS-stimulated monocytes. The effect is mediated by a transient cis-eQTL present only in early LPS response.
biological.sample_size: 226-710 individuals across six blood cell types

biological.citation: Identification of mouse SLC39A8 as the transporter responsible for cadmium-induced toxicity in the testis (PMID: 15722412)
biological.summary: ZIP8 expression in mouse fetal fibroblasts increased Cd influx more than 10-fold and Cd-induced cell death sensitivity 30-fold. In situ hybridization showed ZIP8 mRNA in testicular vascular endothelial cells of Cd-sensitive mouse strains but not resistant strains, identifying Slc39a8 as the Cdm locus.

biological.citation: Generation of a Slc39a8 hypomorph mouse: markedly decreased ZIP8 Zn²⁺/(HCO₃⁻)₂ transporter expression (PMID: 21658371)
biological.summary: ZIP8 functions as an electroneutral Zn2+/(HCO3-)2 symporter. The Slc39a8(neo) hypomorphic allele greatly reduced ZIP8 expression in embryo, fetus and visceral yolk sac of homozygous mice.

biological.citation: MicroRNA-488 regulates zinc transporter SLC39A8/ZIP8 during pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (PMID: 23688035)
biological.summary: miR-488 targets ZIP8 and is decreased in OA chondrocytes. IL-1β suppresses miR-488 while TGF-β3 induces it. Suppressing ZIP8 in an OA animal model reduced cartilage degradation, and miR-488 inhibits MMP-13 activity through ZIP8.

biological.citation: Calcium and the Ca-ATPase SPCA1 modulate plasma membrane abundance of ZIP8 and ZIP14 to regulate Mn(II) uptake in brain microvascular endothelial cells (PMID: 35787370)
biological.summary: In human brain microvascular endothelial cells, SPCA1 knockdown raised cytoplasmic Ca2+, which increased plasma membrane localization of ZIP8 and ZIP14 and 54Mn uptake. SPCA1 overexpression and Ca2+ chelation had the opposite effect, showing that Ca2+ and SPCA1 regulate ZIP8 membrane cycling.
